course_name_original: Certificación Energética y Energías Renovables en la Edificación
course_name_en: Energy Certification and Renewable Energies in Buildings

learning_outcomes.text: Know and apply European Directives and Spanish regulations aimed at energy saving and improving energy efficiency in buildings.
Evaluate geothermal, aerothermal and solar resources available for their use in building thermal systems in a given area or environment.
Design the basic equipment and systems for building thermal installations.

Analyze practical cases of energy evaluation in buildings, assessing the energy savings and CO2 emissions obtained with different technological solutions and, in particular, with the use of renewable resource utilization technologies.
Use simulation software tools to support the study of the thermal behavior of buildings and for energy certification.

syllabus_topics: Evolution in Europe and Spain of energy demand and the use of renewable energies in buildings (European Directives), Spanish Regulations: Technical Building Code (CTE) and Regulation of Thermal Installations in Buildings (RITE).
Methodology for energy certification analysis in buildings. Case studies.
Computer simulation tools for the study of the thermal behavior of buildings.
Renewable technologies in building 1: Heat pump (aerothermal and geothermal) and biomass.
Renewable technologies in building 2: Solar energy.
Thermal energy recovery in ventilation systems and sensible and latent heat storage.
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.15 x (Active Participation) + 0.20 x (Individual Work) + 0.20 x (Laboratory Practices) + 0.45 x (Exam). A final grade of 5 points is required to pass the course. For students in Differentiated Evaluation, the Active Participation grade is replaced by an additional individual work and the Laboratory Practices grade is compensated with an extra exam on the same day as the general exam. In extraordinary calls, the individual work can be maintained from the last ordinary call or a new work can be submitted. The final exam in extraordinary calls includes both the theoretical-practical and laboratory practices parts, with a formula of 0.20 x (Individual Work) + 0.20 x (Laboratory Practices) + 0.60 x (Exam).
